gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Chunky, open-mouthed letters make the text feel friendly and easy to settle into. Noto Sans Old Turkic is the sturdy partner to Warnes, whose stretched, spacious letters taper out like pipe cleaners.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Unica One looks marker-drawn, its curves holding open daylight inside every bend. Noto Sans Marchen backs it with small letters standing almost capital-sized, so the heading keeps the spotlight.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-mayan-nume: Unica One reads like outlines traced in a single width, commanding and distinctive. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals brings lofty-bodied small letters and a gaping c, and that open stance against the outlined heading is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-medefaidri: Commanding and distinctive, Unica One holds a thickness that never shifts with direction. Noto Sans Medefaidrin sits beside it with lowercase that rises high and curves that turn in cleanly, giving the heading a lean, upright partner.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-mende-kika: Distinctive from the first glance, Unica One makes a statement with unvarying strokes. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui does the quieter job, with lowercase that stands up against the capitals and light through every curve.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Unica One has an oversized lowercase, its curves matching the straight stems in thickness, with daylight showing inside every bend. Noto Sans Meroitic, with see-through c openings, reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-mono: Noto Sans Mono reads sturdy, its generously spaced letters never bumping and its curves letting light in. And Unica One, whose thin-looking letters have no thinner parts, lends the headline a commanding edge.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-mro: Unica One's strokes never swell or thin at all. Noto Sans Mro, a sans-serif with dense-looking words and generous entrances into each letter, makes sustained reading feel steady and unhurried.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-multani: Unica One has rounded-wire strokes and an outsized lowercase, with daylight showing inside every curve and a commanding presence. Noto Sans Multani feels lofty beside it, its e leaving a wide gap.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-amiko: Expressive, Warnes stretches out round letters whose outlines never swell or thin. Amiko does the steadier work, with chunky crayon-mark lowercase and terminals that flare outward like a pair of tongs.
